note: Written by the daily Claude review (NEWS-UPDATING.md). items: per-story summary, category, importance and sector scores, keyed by the story id in news.json. extra: stories Claude found itself. brief: today's key points.

points.text: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Voceryq for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy approved in the US and a non-surgical option for a disease usually managed by repeated operations.

The MHRA extended Casgevy's UK authorisation to children aged five and over with severe sickle-cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta-thalassaemia, widening access to gene editing in a younger age group.

AstraZeneca launched a $1.5 billion annual savings programme and said it could mean R&D cuts and shifting trials to emerging markets, while Sanofi said it will seek higher European prices rather than delay launches there.
The US barred imports from three Chinese genomics companies, including BGI Genomics and MGI Tech, under the forced labour import law, cutting off a major source of sequencing supply.

India's CDSCO ordered Sun Pharma to stop making and selling ophthalmic products from an Assam plant after quality system failures, while Gilead placed a partial clinical hold on two CAR-T trials after cases of ICANS.

Merck KGaA opened its new bioprocessing production centre in Korea, a site representing more than €300 million of investment, as SK bioscience joined a BARDA-funded Bundibugyo vaccine manufacturing effort during the DRC outbreak.

diagnostics.why: Repeat variation as a source of disease risk missed by standard genotyping.

pharma.why: Target discovery from cell-type-specific regulation.

ai.why: Large-scale single-cell genomic analysis.

5c0816f0e3a9.summary: Single-neuron sequencing shows genomic abnormalities are common in human cortical neurons before birth but are largely eliminated around birth, pointing to a developmental quality-control step.

healthcare.why: Bears on the origins of neurodevelopmental disorders.

pharma.why: Basic neurogenomics relevant to CNS drug discovery.

227e37875a05.summary: A Nature review sets out the molecular basis of inflammatory rheumatic diseases and the emerging therapeutic concepts aimed at durable disease control.

pharma.why: Target landscape in immunology and inflammation.

f49d7d704cab.summary: Nature paper: excitatory neurons under high-frequency stimulation show a presynaptic form of homeostatic plasticity mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein.

e6217c01c849.summary: Nature paper: losing canonical BAF function increases CTCF and cohesin binding, reshaping 3D genome architecture and reprogramming transcription.

pharma.why: SWI/SNF complexes are mutated in many cancers and are drug targets.

9515d6ca449f.summary: Science News reports that exercise prompts bone cells called osteocytes to secrete proteins that slowed ageing and extended lifespan in mice.

pharma.why: Bone-derived proteins as potential ageing therapeutics.

healthcare.why: Mechanism linking exercise to healthy ageing.

3acc6c635f54.summary: STAT reports that FDA and CMS officials are working behind the scenes to head off a conflict with states that want to regulate or test AI in clinical settings themselves.

ai.why: Who regulates clinical AI in the US is being decided now.

healthcare.why: Affects deployment of AI tools in care.

908b81087a4c.summary: The UK Biobank is gradually reopening to researchers after being closed for much of 2026 following a large data leak.

biosecurity.why: Security of a major human genomic and health dataset.

ai.why: A key training and analysis resource returns for researchers.

healthcare.why: Restores a widely used research dataset.

9f483758494d.summary: Nikon withdrew an AI-generated video said to show primary ciliary dyskinesia, prompting concern about how AI misrepresentation of rare disease can cause harm.

ai.why: AI-generated scientific imagery and its accuracy.

healthcare.why: Rare disease representation in medical media.

6c243766dc48.summary: A UKHSA report found more than 3,000 infants were hospitalised with chickenpox last year, as it urged parents to use the varicella vaccine now part of the NHS childhood programme.

healthcare.why: Burden data behind a new routine childhood vaccination.

biosecurity.why: Vaccine-preventable disease surveillance.

extra.title: Japan's Astellas Pharma inks $400M deal with AI Proteins to develop miniprotein therapeutics
extra.summary: Astellas signed a research collaboration and licence agreement with US computational protein design company AI Proteins, which is eligible for more than $400 million in upfront and milestone payments plus royalties. AI Proteins will design miniproteins against several targets and Astellas takes an exclusive worldwide licence to the candidates.

ai.why: De novo computational protein design backed by a large pharma deal.

pharma.why: Japanese pharma buys into a new therapeutic modality.

investment.why: $400M+ in potential payments for a private AI biotech.

extra.title: Singapore launches national reference to guide clinical investigations of medical devices
extra.summary: Singapore published Technical Reference TR 151:2026 on clinical investigation of medical devices, setting out what a device study application should contain and how to apply ISO 14155:2026 locally. It is meant to make ethics review more predictable, since most existing trial guidance was written for medicines.

meddevices.why: Clear national rules for running device trials in Singapore.

diagnostics.why: Applies to diagnostic devices studied clinically.

extra.title: Singapore's biopharma manufacturers launch S$4.8M study award for manufacturing careers
extra.summary: The Biopharmaceutical Manufacturers' Advisory Council launched a S$4.8 million study award expected to reach about 1,000 polytechnic and ITE students over five years, with cash awards of S$3,000-5,000 and priority internships at member companies.

bioprocessing.why: Workforce pipeline for biopharma manufacturing in a major hub.

pharma.why: Industry investment in local skills.

extra.title: Samsung Bioepis targets 20 biosimilars by 2030, eyes ADC and obesity drugs
extra.summary: Samsung Bioepis plans to grow from 11 marketed biosimilars to 20 by 2030 and is eyeing ADCs and obesity drugs; it filed in Korea in August for SB27, a Keytruda biosimilar.

pharma.why: Biosimilar pipeline targets originals with about 114 trillion won in 2025 sales, including Keytruda.

bioprocessing.why: Expansion by one of the largest biologics manufacturing groups.

extra.title: ECDC update: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, multi-country, 2026
extra.summary: ECDC updated its tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak on 26 October: DRC had reported 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 related deaths across eight provinces by 18 October, and Nigeria reported a case on 20 October in a traveller from Uganda, with 53 contacts identified.

biosecurity.why: Large Ebola outbreak now with exported cases in Nigeria and Kenya.

healthcare.why: Major public health emergency in Africa with imported-case risk elsewhere.

pharma.why: No licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo virus; trials are under way.

diagnostics.why: Need for testing at borders and in affected countries.

extra.title: Kaigene signs agreement worth up to $580M with Korea's Celltrion for anti-APRIL antibody KG013
extra.summary: Celltrion took exclusive worldwide rights to Kaigene's half-life-extended anti-APRIL antibody KG013, initially for IgA nephropathy; Kaigene is eligible for up to $580.5 million including an undisclosed upfront and milestones, plus royalties.

pharma.why: Korean biologics giant buys into a novel antibody for a hot kidney disease target.

investment.why: Up to $580M deal for a US biotech.

extra.title: Waters and Labcorp to expand access to cervical cancer screening
extra.summary: Labcorp and Waters will offer the FDA-approved BD Onclarity HPV assay, which separately identifies six high-risk HPV types, through Labcorp's US network from late 2026, including its consumer channel.

diagnostics.why: Extended HPV genotyping rolled out by a national lab.

healthcare.why: Aims to close the US cervical screening gap.

extra.title: Enhertu approved in the EU as adjuvant treatment for patients with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment for HER2-positive early breast cancer
extra.summary: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu for HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment. AstraZeneca says in the DESTINY-Breast05 phase 3 trial it cut the risk of invasive recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 (3-year IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%).

pharma.why: Moves a leading ADC into the curative early-disease setting in Europe.

healthcare.why: Changes standard care for high-risk early breast cancer patients.

extra.title: Korea's biohealth exports hit record $24.8 billion as cosmetics surge 31%
extra.summary: South Korea's biohealth exports rose 19.4% to a record $24.75B in the first nine months of 2026, per KHIDI; pharmaceuticals grew 14.2% to $8.93B, led by biopharmaceuticals at $5.71B, while pharma exports to the US fell 30%.

pharma.why: Korean biologics and biosimilar exports keep growing.

bioprocessing.why: Reflects Korea's CDMO and biosimilar manufacturing scale.

extra.title: Asundexian first Factor XIa inhibitor approved in China for stroke risk reduction after priority review
extra.summary: China approved Bayer's once-daily asundexian (Sunharbo) to reduce stroke risk after non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or high-risk TIA, the first approval for a Factor XIa inhibitor; Bayer says it cut ischaemic stroke by 26% without more bleeding in the 12,327-patient OCEANIC-STROKE trial.

pharma.why: First-ever approval for the Factor XIa class of blood thinners.

healthcare.why: New secondary stroke prevention option without added bleeding.

investment.why: Key growth asset for Bayer; other filings under review.

extra.title: Korea to Nurture 200 Pharma and Biotech Ventures by 2030
extra.summary: South Korea's health and SME ministries launched the K-Pharma-Bio Frontier Company programme, selecting 50 ventures a year to reach 200 by 2030, with 60 billion won of investment and 90 billion won of guarantees over three years.

investment.why: State capital and guarantees for Korean biotech startups.

pharma.why: 40% of slots go to new drug developers.

meddevices.why: 20 slots for digital health and device firms.

bioprocessing.why: 10 slots for biomaterials and production technology.

extra.title: Australia's Audax Biosciences inks immuno-oncology deal worth $1.34 B with Astellas Pharma
extra.summary: Astellas took an exclusive option and licence on DAX-044, Australian biotech Audax Biosciences' IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusion, paying $285 million in upfront and option payments with up to $1.05 billion in milestones plus royalties; Audax will run a phase 1 study expected to start in 2027.

pharma.why: Large option deal for an engineered cytokine in oncology.

investment.why: Australian biotech lands a $1.34 billion-value agreement with a Japanese major.

extra.title: PDRadiopharma injects JPY 16.5 B into new manufacturing facility in Japan
extra.summary: PeptiDream's subsidiary PDRadiopharma will spend about 16.5 billion yen on a radiopharmaceutical plant at Kazusa Akademia Park in Chiba, with construction starting in 2027 and completion in 2028, for domestic supply and Asia-Pacific exports.

bioprocessing.why: New radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capacity in Japan.

pharma.why: Supply base for a fast-growing radioligand therapy market.

investment.why: Large capital commitment funded by bank loans and incentives.

extra.title: Singapore approves Merck's CAPVAXIVE 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine
extra.summary: Singapore's Health Sciences Authority has approved Merck's 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine CAPVAXIVE for adults aged 18 and over, covering serotypes responsible for most invasive pneumococcal disease in adults.

pharma.why: Asian market access for a next-generation adult pneumococcal vaccine.

healthcare.why: Wider adult pneumococcal protection in Singapore.

extra.title: GC Biopharma gets MFDS approval for Hunterase ICV
extra.summary: Korea's MFDS approved GC Biopharma's Hunterase ICV, an enzyme therapy injected into the brain's ventricles for Hunter syndrome patients with central nervous system symptoms; the company says it is the first treatment approved in Korea for those symptoms, used alongside the intravenous form.

pharma.why: Intracerebroventricular delivery solves the blood-brain barrier problem for an enzyme therapy.

healthcare.why: First Korean option for neurological Hunter syndrome.

extra.title: Indian regulators order Sun Pharma to halt eye-drug production at Assam plant over quality lapses
extra.summary: India's CDSCO and the Assam drugs controller ordered Sun Pharma to stop making, selling and distributing ophthalmic products from its Kokjhar plant in Assam after a joint inspection found quality management system failures, naming products including Lotepred, Nepalact OD, Nepalact-Z, Brinzotim and Depopred. Production cannot resume until a satisfactory compliance report is accepted; the company has filed one and regulators are reviewing it.

pharma.why: Manufacturing halt at India's largest drugmaker over GMP failures.

healthcare.why: Supply of several prescription eye medicines is suspended.

bioprocessing.why: Sterile ophthalmic manufacturing quality systems under scrutiny.

extra.title: DKSH to acquire NewBridge Pharmaceuticals for $390 million to build a MENA healthcare platform
extra.summary: DKSH agreed to buy 100% of Dubai-based NewBridge Pharmaceuticals at an enterprise value of $390 million, extending its healthcare outsourcing business beyond Asia Pacific into 14 Middle East and North Africa markets. NewBridge, which provides market access, medical affairs and sales services for specialty and rare disease medicines, is expected to post net sales of about $385 million in 2027 at a high single-digit EBITDA margin.

pharma.why: Commercialisation route for specialty and rare disease drugs in MENA.

investment.why: $390m enterprise value acquisition expanding a distribution platform.

healthcare.why: Market access infrastructure for innovative medicines in the region.

extra.title: Waters builds AI peak integration into Empower chromatography software
extra.summary: Waters added AI-powered peak integration to Empower, its chromatography data system for regulated laboratories, saying it cuts manual effort and variability in late-stage development and QC while keeping data inside the validated environment. Early access enrolment starts in December 2026 and validated deployment is expected in mid-2027; Waters says the strategy targets around 500,000 Empower users.

ai.why: AI embedded in a regulated GxP data system rather than a research tool.

bioprocessing.why: Analytical QC workflows in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

pharma.why: Late-stage development and release testing.
